---
title: "Part 4 – Explore, declare, publish"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/one-day-tools.html#/part-4-explore-declare-publish){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 4 opens the menu of alternatives to the specification you reproduced, has you explore it and put a dot on the class chart, then asks for the one analysis you would defend, declared before it runs. The last stretch covers where a finished reanalysis is archived, and what a version history, a licence and a registration each add to the chance that someone else can find and re-run it.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Specification menu](../../exercise/spec-menu.qmd) and slides | The axes you choose from, the three levels they sort into, what the constrained task left open, the one-deviation rule and the claim-alignment convention that puts every result on one scale. | 15 minutes |
| Task 4 in the workspace or on the [Browser lab](../../exercise/browser-lab.qmd), then [Multiverse](../../results.qmd) | Call `try_spec()` three or four times, changing one argument at a time, print them with `my_experiments()`, then submit the one you would defend with `submit_exploration()`. Your dot is drawn on the chart as an open circle. | 20 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../results.qmd) and slides | The exploratory dots from the class, read against the full curve and the five analysts. | 12 minutes |
| Slides | The critics of multiverse analysis, the argument that a fully specified question has one correct analysis, and what preregistration settles and what it leaves open. | 8 minutes |
| Slides, archiving and registering, with [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) and [Social science data sources](../../companion/data-sources.qmd) as the companions | The three addresses connected with the case and what each of them is for; the registered protocol that Multi100 itself filed; the two preregistration templates, and the eight questions of the shorter one with your answers already mapped onto them. | 12 minutes |
| The report skeleton in the workspace, or [Browser lab](../../exercise/browser-lab.qmd) Task 5 | Complete the preregistration block before you run anything, translate it into model syntax yourself, run it, render the report, and submit with `report_result()`. Your declared result is drawn on the chart as a filled circle. | 18 minutes |
| Slides | Two sentences worth keeping, and what you take with you. | 5 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have an exploratory dot and a declared dot on the class chart, a rendered report that contains a preregistration block with its result underneath, and the addresses at which a reanalysis like yours is archived and registered.
